summary.brief: A man installs a water‑softening system in his RV, showing the parts, mounting, plumbing, and testing.
summary.detailed: The presenter begins by laying out the required plumbing parts—pipe, crimper, crimp rings, elbows and adapters. He removes the existing spinner panel, finds unused space behind the wall, and prepares a mounting location by installing two 2 × 4 boards between the storage walls and securing them with a ratchet strap. He cuts the water‑inlet pipe, routes it through the new softener before the existing filtration unit, and adds a main‑water shut‑off valve for future access. After connecting all fittings, he runs water to flush the system, checks that the line is pressurised and leak‑free, secures the hoses with zip ties, and finally reinstalls the panel cover, completing the installation.

action.detailed: Mount the softener on a braced 2 × 4 frame, cut and connect the inlet pipe through the unit, attach a shut‑off valve, flush the system, verify pressure and absence of leaks, secure the hoses with zip ties, and replace the panel cover.

summary_sent_to_llm.title: RV Water Softener Install
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The presenter begins by laying out the required plumbing parts—pipe, crimper, crimp rings, elbows and adapters. He removes the existing spinner panel, finds unused space behind the wall, and prepares a mounting location by installing two 2 × 4 boards between the storage walls and securing them with a ratchet strap. He cuts the water‑inlet pipe, routes it through the new softener before the existing filtration unit, and adds a main‑water shut‑off valve for future access. After connecting all fittings, he runs water to flush the system, checks that the line is pressurised and leak‑free, secures the hoses with zip ties, and finally reinstalls the panel cover, completing the installation.
action_list: Walk and point at plumbing components
Point and activate the water‑softener tank
adjust valves and operate a lever on the water‑filter tank
Operate valves and demonstrate pipe connections
Point and pan over tools and wiring

llm.system_prompt:
You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to either of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   A video can match neither, one, or both. Be strict — when in doubt,
   say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
